This method works for zonal, ivy, regal and scented geraniums, and suits Indian balcony and terrace gardens.
Geraniums are among the easiest flowering plants to multiply. One healthy mother plant can give you 10–20 new plants every season. No seeds, no expensive saplings, just one cutting and the right technique.
🌱 What you'll learn in this video:
✅ The best time to take geranium cuttings in India
✅ How to choose a healthy stem for propagation
✅ The correct cutting length and where to cut (node method)
✅ Why you should remove lower leaves and flower buds
✅ Callusing: why drying the cut end prevents rot
✅ Rooting hormone: is it needed? (Natural options: honey, aloe vera, cinnamon)
✅ The best soil mix for fast rooting
✅ Soil vs water propagation: which works better?
✅ Watering, light and care until roots form
✅ When and how to transplant your new geranium plant
✅ Common mistakes that cause cuttings to rot
🗓️ Best season for geranium propagation in India:
February–March and September–November are ideal. Avoid the peak monsoon, when humidity causes stem rot, and extreme summer heat.
🪴 Quick method summary:
1️⃣ Take a 4–6 inch healthy, non-flowering tip cutting just below a node.
2️⃣ Remove the lower leaves, keeping only 2–3 at the top. Pinch off any buds.
3️⃣ Let the cut end dry and callus for a few hours.
4️⃣ Dip it in rooting hormone (optional).
5️⃣ Plant it in a well-draining mix of cocopeat + perlite or sand.
6️⃣ Keep it in bright, indirect light. Water lightly and avoid overwatering.
7️⃣ Roots form in about 2–4 weeks. New leaf growth means success! 🎉
⚠️ Important tip: Don't cover geranium cuttings with plastic. Unlike many plants, geraniums dislike high humidity and can rot quickly.

A black base can come from soggy mix, too much hormone, or actual rot: same symptom, different causes, different fixes.

Tell me in the comments what you're rooting and which USDA zone you're in. I want to see which zones are dealing with the soggy-mix problem right now.

Dip the bottom end of the rose stem into a rooting hormone powder (like "Cutting Aid"). This stimulates rapid root growth.
Step 3: The Honey Dip
Dip the powdered end of the stem into pure honey. Honey acts as a natural antibacterial and antifungal agent, protecting the cutting from rot while it roots!

Plant the treated cutting into a clear plastic cup filled with moist, well-draining potting soil. The clear cup is the secret weapon—it lets you monitor the root development!

Want unlimited geranium plants for free? 🌸 In this video, you'll learn how to propagate geraniums (Pelargonium) from stem cuttings, step by step, with a high success rate. This method works for zonal, ivy, regal and scented geraniums, and suits Indian balcony and terrace gardens.
Geraniums are among the easiest flowering plants to multiply. One healthy mother plant can give you 10–20 new plants every season. No seeds, no expensive saplings, just one cutting and the right technique.
🌱 What you'll learn in this video:
✅ The best time to take geranium cuttings in India
✅ How to choose a healthy stem for propagation
✅ The correct cutting length and where to cut (node method)
✅ Why you should remove lower leaves and flower buds
✅ Callusing: why drying the cut end prevents rot
✅ Rooting hormone: is it needed? (Natural options: honey, aloe vera, cinnamon)
✅ The best soil mix for fast rooting
✅ Soil vs water propagation: which works better?
✅ Watering, light and care until roots form
✅ When and how to transplant your new geranium plant
✅ Common mistakes that cause cuttings to rot
🗓️ Best season for geranium propagation in India:
February–March and September–November are ideal. Avoid the peak monsoon, when humidity causes stem rot, and extreme summer heat.
🪴 Quick method summary:
1️⃣ Take a 4–6 inch healthy, non-flowering tip cutting just below a node.
2️⃣ Remove the lower leaves, keeping only 2–3 at the top. Pinch off any buds.
3️⃣ Let the cut end dry and callus for a few hours.
4️⃣ Dip it in rooting hormone (optional).
5️⃣ Plant it in a well-draining mix of cocopeat + perlite or sand.
6️⃣ Keep it in bright, indirect light. Water lightly and avoid overwatering.
7️⃣ Roots form in about 2–4 weeks. New leaf growth means success! 🎉
⚠️ Important tip: Don't cover geranium cuttings with plastic. Unlike many plants, geraniums dislike high humidity and can rot quickly.

results.title: Cuttings Turning Black? Do This Before You Lose the Whole Batch

Black, mushy base on your cuttings? Most people grab more rooting hormone, but that can make the problem worse. A black base can come from soggy mix, too much hormone, or actual rot: same symptom, different causes, different fixes.

In this video I go through what to check, in order, for soft-stemmed fall cuttings like geraniums, coleus and begonias. It takes about ten minutes and things you probably already have. I also flag where the research is solid and where it doesn't translate perfectly to a cutting on your kitchen counter.

What you'll learn:
- How to read the base: firm and pale vs dark and soft
- Why to cut just below a node
- Why air in your mix matters more than water (and how to squeeze-test it)
- Perlite, vermiculite or sand for rot-prone cuttings like geraniums
- Why easy cuttings often don't need rooting hormone
- How to use hormone without contaminating the jar
- Venting the dome and reading the condensation
- Fungus gnats, sticky traps and cleaning your blade

results.title: Grow Roses from Cuttings Using HONEY! 🍯 Insane Roots in 45 Days 🌹#garden #rose #shorts
results.description:
Want to know the secret to propagating roses 🌹 with massive root systems? 🌿 In this video, I show you a simple, highly effective trick using everyday items to grow beautiful rose plants from cuttings in just 45 days! Using clear plastic cups lets you watch the magic happen as the roots take over.
Here is the exact step-by-step process shown in the video:
✂️ Step 1: Prepare the Cutting
Take a healthy rose stem and cut it to about 6-8 inches. Remove all the lower leaves and thorns, and make a clean, angled cut at the top to prevent water from pooling.
Step 2: Apply Rooting Hormone
Dip the bottom end of the rose stem into a rooting hormone powder (like "Cutting Aid"). This stimulates rapid root growth.
Step 3: The Honey Dip
Dip the powdered end of the stem into pure honey. Honey acts as a natural antibacterial and antifungal agent, protecting the cutting from rot while it roots!
🥤 Step 4: Plant in Clear Cups
Plant the treated cutting into a clear plastic cup filled with moist, well-draining potting soil. The clear cup is the secret weapon—it lets you monitor the root development!
💦 Step 5: Water & Wait
Mist the soil thoroughly with a spray bottle to keep it consistently moist (but not soggy). Place it in bright, indirect sunlight.
⏳ Step 6: The 45-Day Reveal
After 45 days, check the results! You’ll see incredible, thick white roots filling the cup and beautiful new leaves sprouting at the top.

Два проверенных способа — и оба рабочие! Но нюансы есть:

💧 Вода:
Плюс — визуальный контроль (сразу видно, когда появляются корешки).

Плюс — корни сразу растут в "родной" среде, адаптация после пересадки легче.
Минус — сложно контролировать влажность.

Мой вердикт: Для осени выбираю торф + фитолампа. Корни получаются коренастыми, не водянистыми.
